The author's proof (source lines 835-854) is a structure-identity computation: the identity type of precategories is unfolded into an object-type identity, hom-type identities after transport, and two coherence identities for units and composition (lines 836-843), the coherences being harmless because the identity types of hom-sets are mere propositions (line 844); univalence then converts the componentwise identities into equivalences, which is precisely the data of an isomorphism of categories (lines 845-851); and the final line records that the equivalence on display is the one induced by identity elimination (lines 852-853). The statement gives the two types and nothing else, and the proof (source lines 906-923) has to build both directions: on the one hand it must produce, from a functor on the product, its fibres at each object of A together with the natural transformations induced by the morphisms of A; on the other hand it must define the action on pairs of morphisms and notice that the two candidate composites agree by naturality of the given functor; and finally it must observe that the two constructions are inverse. The author explicitly defers the functoriality checks and the inverse verification as easy or clear, which this card records verbatim, so what is counted is the pair of constructions and the naturality observation, not those routine verifications.

The 46-line proof builds a quasi-inverse in both directions and then checks two round trips that live in different types, so neither can be waved through. The direction from representability must invent the functor action G(g) := gamma_{Gb,b'}(g o eps_b) together with eta_a := gamma_{a,Fa}(1_{Fa}) and eps_b := inverse gamma_{Gb,b}(1_{Gb}) (lines 1022-1025); the reverse direction must produce the whole family gamma from G and eta with inverse built from F and eps, using the triangle identities (lines 1028-1039). The first round trip is a rewrite of G(f) o eta_a that consumes naturality of gamma (lines 1041-1049), and the second recovers the hom-action of G from G(g o eps_b) o eta_{Gb} = G(g) and then re-derives eta and eps from their defining clauses (lines 1051-1061). removed_items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
removed_items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file brauer.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
removed_items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects basic facts about modules over a finite algebra: there is a simple module, every nonzero module has a simple submodule, a simple module is finite dimensional, and the endomorphism ring of a simple module is a skew field (statement lines 336-346). The proof is a complete argument: the first assertion follows from the second because the algebra is a nonzero module over itself, and the second holds by taking a submodule of minimal finite dimension, whose existence is guaranteed by cyclicity (proof lines 348-351); finite dimensionality of a simple module follows from the submodule generated by an element (proof lines 352-353); and a nonzero endomorphism of a simple module is injective and hence an isomorphism, which makes its endomorphism ring a skew field (proof lines 353-354). The non-formal content is the minimal dimensional submodule argument. The claim is H2.

removed_items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finite central skew field of degree d, every finite splitting field has degree over the ground field divisible by d (statement lines 906-911). The proof is a complete argument: the characterization of splitting fields produces an algebra in the same Brauer class whose degree is the square of the degree of the splitting field (proof lines 913-916), and by similarity that algebra is a matrix algebra over the skew field, so its degree is the size of the matrix times the degree of the skew field; comparing and taking square roots gives the divisibility (proof lines 917-919). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two degree computations. The claim is H2.
